sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Peshawar School Roof Collapse Kills 33, Mostly Children
cards.content: At least 33 people, including 32 children and one teacher, were killed when a school roof collapsed in Peshawar, Pakistan. The disaster occurred during class, trapping students under debris. The building's owner was arrested, and police promised a thorough investigation into building code violations. cards.title: Houthi missile attack kills two in Yemen's presidential palace
cards.content: Two security personnel were killed and many others injured in a Houthi missile attack on the presidential palace in Aden, Yemen. The attack, which also targeted the prime minister and other ministers, was condemned by Yemen's Prime Minister Shaya Zindani, who called it 'cowardly' and vowed the government would continue operations against the Houthis.

cards.title: Israel Accused of Killing 254 in Gaza, Lebanon, West Bank, and Israel
cards.content: The Israeli military has been accused of killing or injuring 254 people in Gaza, Lebanon, the West Bank, and Israel, but has not publicly concluded investigations into most of these incidents. Using AI tools, BBC Verify found that the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) said it was investigating each incident, but only 28 had public outcomes. The IDF has stated that it takes every allegation seriously and conducts investigations, but critics say the lack of transparency and accountability undermines the rule of law. The International Committee of the Red Cross emphasizes that investigations into potential violations of international humanitarian law should be as transparent as possible. Many incidents, including the killing of 93 people, including 11 children, in an air strike on a school building in Gaza, remain under investigation.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Tesla Reveals Next-Gen Roadster Details on Thursday
cards.content: Tesla is set to show off its long-delayed next-generation Roadster on Thursday, almost a decade after taking deposits. The event will be livestreamed from a SpaceX test site in Texas, where executives will disclose pricing, details, and production targets. The high-end, low-volume model relies on SpaceX technology to enable it to hover.

cards.title: Apple and Meta team up on AI, release open model for developers
cards.content: Apple and Meta, rivals for years, are collaborating on artificial intelligence. They've released a new AI model, Muse Spark Open, that developers can run on Apple's high-end desktop computers. This model is open-weight, meaning developers can download and use it on various hardware. The collaboration aims to make AI more accessible and secure, and could signal a deeper relationship between the two companies.

cards.title: TSMC Struggles to Meet AI Chip Demand Despite Record Profits
cards.content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, the world's leading chip manufacturer, is struggling to keep up with demand for AI chips. Despite record profits, the company can't produce enough chips to meet customer needs. This shortage could impact the entire industry's ability to scale, as tech firms rely on TSMC for custom AI accelerators. With many companies vying for a piece of the action, competition is extremely fierce, and TSMC is working to bring more capacity online.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: NYU Researchers Identify Seven Biomarkers in Human Milk Linked to Nutrition and Infant Growth
cards.content: Researchers at NYU Grossman School of Medicine identified seven biomarkers in human milk that are linked to maternal nutrition, infant growth, and mammary gland function. The study, published in Science, analyzed over 1,500 milk samples from diverse populations and used multi-omics analysis to examine various molecular components. The findings suggest that human milk composition is not fixed, but rather influenced by maternal nutrition, and that some components respond to supplementation. The study's senior author, Liat Shenhav, emphasized the importance of understanding mammary function and milk composition to support maternal and infant health.

cards.title: Saline injections ease carpal tunnel symptoms for six months
cards.content: A small study suggests that injecting saline into the wrist to relieve carpal tunnel symptoms can provide lasting relief, without using steroids. The study, published in Radiology, found that the procedure, called nerve hydrodissection, can reduce symptoms and pain for at least six months. The procedure uses ultrasound guidance to inject a small amount of saline around the affected nerve, and it was well-tolerated by patients. The study's findings indicate that hydrodissection may be a safe and minimally invasive treatment option for mild to moderate carpal tunnel syndrome, and it could potentially delay or even eliminate the need for surgery.

cards.title: Gene helps gut bacterium survive hospital disinfectants
cards.content: A newly discovered antibiotic resistance gene helps a harmful gut bacterium, Clostridioides difficile, build tougher spores that can survive hospital disinfectants. This gene, found by Monash University researchers, allows the bacterium to produce spores that can withstand hospital-grade cleaning products and high temperatures, making infections harder to control and allowing resistant strains to spread more easily.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: World Exceeds Seven Planetary Boundaries, Report Says
cards.content: According to a recent report, the world has exceeded seven out of nine planetary boundaries, which regulate the health of the planet. The four most transgressed boundaries include climate change, damage to ecosystems, changes to natural processes, and the introduction of new substances like plastic. Three boundaries have been crossed, while two remain within safe limits. A climate scientist notes that the report is global in scope, but regional variations can be seen, with strong pressures in South Asia and India.

cards.title: Northern India Braces for Heavy Rainfall and Thunderstorms
cards.content: Heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, hailstorms, and gusty winds are forecasted for several regions in northern India, including Delhi-NCR, Punjab, Haryana, and Chandigarh, with orange alerts issued by the India Meteorological Department. Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry are expected to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall as the northeast monsoon develops. Residents are advised to monitor official updates, exercise caution, and follow local advisories amid concerns over waterlogging, traffic congestion, lightning strikes, and crop damage.

cards.title: Indonesia Reports 1.06 Million Wildfire Hotspots, 896,000 Hectares Burned
cards.content: As of October 14 Indonesia has detected over 1.06 million wildfire hotspots surpassing the 885000 recorded in 2019. So far nearly 896000 hectares of land have burned mostly due to dry conditions and slash-and-burn practices. The situation is made worse by the ongoing Super El Niño which could make the fires harder to control and increase the risk of new outbreaks. Smoke from the fires has already spread to neighboring Malaysia and Singapore affecting air quality and public health.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: La Bola Negra Nominated for Best Picture Academy Awards
cards.content: A film called La Bola Negra is a contender for the Academy Awards' best picture prize. The movie tells three stories of gay men across a century in Spain exploring themes of love repression and self-punishment. The film has received critical acclaim and is a commercial hit in Spain. It's known for its beautiful visuals complex storyline and courage in showing sexual desire. The directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi have been praised for their work and the film's cast including Álvaro Lafuente Calvo and Carlos González have also received recognition.

cards.title: Lena Dunham Revives Girls for Limited Run with Original Cast
cards.content: Lena Dunham the creator of the popular TV show Girls announced that the show will return for a limited run after a 10-year hiatus. The revival will feature five episodes and reunite the original cast including Allison Williams Jemima Kirke Zosia Mamet and Andrew Rannells. Dunham said she's been missing the characters and that they started talking to her again around her 40th birthday. The show will explore what's happened to the characters since they were in their 20s.

cards.title: Rob Brydon Voices New Animated "The Baddies" Adaptation
cards.content: Welsh actor Rob Brydon is voicing a new animated adaptation of the popular children's book "The Baddies" over the Christmas period. The story follows a troll a ghost and a witch as they try to steal a blue spotty hanky from a brave little girl. Brydon will be joined by Gavin and Stacey co-stars Sheridan Smith and Alison Steadman as well as Hammed Animashaun Robyn Cara and Francesca Mills. The half-hour special celebrates kindness and standing up to bullies and features beautiful animation.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: UK Banks Face Budget Target with £15bn Profits
cards.content: Banking executives expect the sector to be targeted in the upcoming budget, as the UK's biggest banks made around £15bn in profit in the first half of the year. The sector has contributed nearly £40bn to the Treasury and paid a surcharge on corporation tax. There are several ways the chancellor could extract more money from the banks, including raising the surcharge or changing a tax rule that allows banks to offset past losses against profits.

cards.title: UK Economy Defies Forecasts, Grows by 0.1%
cards.content: UK Chancellor John Healey has hailed the country's economy as resilient after it grew by 0.1% in August, defying forecasts of a slight contraction. The growth was driven by an increase in production, including manufacturing, oil and gas extraction, and energy supply. The services sector was flat, while construction contracted. Healey has promised to use the budget to provide relief from cost of living and cost of business pressures, but did not elaborate on specific measures.

cards.title: Government to Review Airport Drop-Off Charges After Prices Rise
cards.content: The government has agreed to review airport drop-off charges after prices rose by a third since summer 2025. Major UK airports like Gatwick and Stansted have seen fees jump from £7 to £10 while Edinburgh and Bournemouth airports have also increased their charges. The Department for Transport wants to ensure travel remains accessible and that passengers are treated fairly. The RAC a motoring organization has been campaigning against the increases saying they are a growing source of anger and frustration for drivers.
